output.rationale: Start with a simple cause map, then use two teaching blocks and immediate retrieval to build the WWI timeline in order.

coverage.focus: WWI cause map: prewar tensions, outbreak sequence, and basic 1914 to 1918 chronology.
essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made a wider war more likely by splitting Europe into rival blocs.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, which moved through Austrian action, German support, and wider mobilization to declarations of war.
Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 runs from the Sarajevo crisis to the war’s start, U.S. entry, and the armistice.
completionEvidence: Name the main alliance blocs and at least three prewar tensions.
Put Sarajevo, the July Crisis, the start of the war, U.S. entry, and the armistice in order.
Explain each uncertain idea as a cause, event, or consequence.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a compact model, explain it in your own words, repair what is missing, then explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: It builds a clear story first, then checks whether you can restate the key relations from memory.
how: Study the short model for the current step.
Close it and explain the idea in plain language.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix any gap.
methodBriefing.completion: You complete the sequence by producing the idea accurately, then repairing and restating it.
personalization: Use the concrete example to anchor the model.
Keep the timeline in order as you explain.

activities.label: Model the cause map
activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: Open the model and study the cause map.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made a wider war more likely by splitting Europe into rival blocs.

activities.label: Explain the outbreak
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Answer in your own words. Then compare your answer with the model.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The Sarajevo assassination set off the July Crisis, then Austria-Hungary acted, Germany backed it, and the crisis widened into declarations of war and general mobilization.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the triggering event and the escalation steps that turned the crisis into war.

activities.label: Repair the chain
activities.title: Fix the escalation chain
activities.body: Correct the sequence if anything is missing. Give one revised version.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The assassination alone directly caused every country to go to war, with no important crisis steps in between.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination did not instantly cause every declaration of war; the July Crisis included Austrian action, German support, mobilization, and then declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that several escalation steps came between the assassination and the wider war.

activities.label: Restate the timeline
activities.title: WWI 1914 to 1918
activities.body: Explain the timeline again in plain language. Keep it in order.
activities.correctAnswer: The war begins in 1914 after the Sarajevo crisis, the fighting continues through 1918, the United States enters in 1917, and the armistice ends the war in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete answer places the major dates in order and identifies the armistice as the end point.

activities.label: Check the whole map
activities.title: Big picture check
activities.body: Choose the best summary of the war’s outbreak and timeline.
choices: Rival alliances and tensions made Europe fragile, the Sarajevo assassination sparked a crisis that escalated into war, and the timeline runs from 1914 to the 1918 armistice.
The war began because the armistice in 1918 triggered the Sarajevo assassination and then the July Crisis.
Europe had no major tensions before 1914, so the war started suddenly with one event and ended in 1914.
The United States entered the war first, and that caused the assassination and the alliance blocs.
activities.correctAnswer: Rival alliances and tensions made Europe fragile, the Sarajevo assassination sparked a crisis that escalated into war, and the timeline runs from 1914 to the 1918 armistice.
activities.feedback: The correct summary links prewar tensions, the July Crisis, and the 1914 to 1918 timeline in order.

items.essentialIdea: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided powers into rival blocs before 1914.

check.title: European Bloc Rivalries
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances shape tensions before 1914?
check.referenceAnswer: They divided Europe into rival alliance blocs, making a local crisis more likely to spread. These alliances raised suspicion and linked states to each other's conflicts.
check.feedback: Correct: the alliances turned tension into bloc rivalry, not peacekeeping.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered Austria-Hungary's ultimatum and the chain of war declarations.

check.title: From Assassination to War
check.prompt: What immediate chain of events followed the Sarajevo assassination?
check.referenceAnswer: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, then war declarations spread as allies mobilized and entered the conflict. The assassination set off the diplomatic crisis that became war.
check.feedback: Correct: the key point is the ultimatum and escalating declarations, not the assassination alone.

items.essentialIdea: 1914 to 1918 covers World War I from outbreak to armistice.

check.title: World War I Timeline
check.prompt: What does the period 1914 to 1918 identify in European history?
check.referenceAnswer: It identifies World War I, beginning in 1914 and ending with the armistice in 1918. The dates mark the war's basic chronology.
check.feedback: Correct: the range names the war's start and end years.

independentCheck.title: War Dates in Context
independentCheck.prompt: Which period matches the basic chronology of World War I?
independentCheck.referenceAnswer: 1914 to 1918. That is the standard date range for World War I.
independentCheck.feedback: Correct: those years frame the war from outbreak to armistice.

recognitionCheck.title: World War I Dates
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which date range matches the basic chronology of World War I?
recognitionCheck.feedback: Correct: World War I is dated 1914 to 1918.
